name: Horseshoe Bay & the Highland Lakes
summary: The Hill Country's lake district — a constant-level lake in a granite basin, a river-carved cavern that was a Confederate powder mill and later a dance hall, and the pink granite quarry that built the Texas Capitol.
seasonalTip: This leg runs in spring, which is the entire point of being here: the Willow City Loop and the roadsides along RR 1431 are the best bluebonnet country in Texas, and peak bloom is usually the first three weeks of April.

lodging.name: Horseshoe Bay Resort, or a rental on Lake LBJ
lodging.blurb: The resort has the marina and three Robert Trent Jones Sr. courses; the rentals have docks.

foodMustTry.name: Pie at the Bluebonnet Cafe
foodMustTry.blurb: In Marble Falls since 1929. Order it by the slice at three in the afternoon, when they do half-price pie happy hour.

foodMustTry.name: A lakeside patio at sunset
foodMustTry.blurb: Lake LBJ faces the right way and the granite hills go pink with it.

days.label: Day 345 — Lake LBJ
days.summary: A day on the water in a granite bowl.

item.title: Lake LBJ & the Horseshoe Bay marina

location.name: Horseshoe Bay Marina, Lake LBJ
location.address: 200 Bay West Blvd, Horseshoe Bay, TX

item.blurb: Lake LBJ is a constant-level lake — the dams at either end hold it within a few inches all year, which is why the Highland Lakes have docks and the rest of Texas has mudflats by August. Rent a boat, swim off it, or paddle up into the granite coves. The water is clear and green and the hills come down to it.

rest.label: The rest of the day is the lake
rest.note: Nothing after this. You have been moving through Texas since Tulsa — the Alamo, the River Walk, the missions — and this is the first stop on the leg that exists to be sat still in. Find a dock facing west.

days.label: Day 346 — Caverns, Granite & Bluebonnets
days.summary: Underground, then the quarry that built the capitol, then the back roads.

item.title: Longhorn Cavern State Park
item.blurb: Carved by a river rather than dripped into being, so it has smooth flowing walls instead of the usual spikes — and a strange history to match. The Confederacy made gunpowder in it, outlaws are supposed to have hidden in it, and in the 1920s somebody put a dance floor and a speakeasy down there. The CCC cleared it out by hand in the 1930s.
gear: a layer — it is 68°F down there year-round

item.title: Marble Falls & Granite Mountain
item.blurb: A dome of solid pink granite on the edge of town, still quarried. The Texas Capitol you walked through on day 327 is built out of it — the state traded a Panhandle ranch's worth of land for the stone and laid a railroad out here to move it. Then pie at the Bluebonnet Cafe, which has been on US-281 since 1929.

item.title: The Willow City Loop
item.blurb: Thirteen miles of one-lane ranch road southwest toward Fredericksburg, and in April it is the most photographed stretch of wildflowers in America — bluebonnets and Indian paintbrush wall to wall down the draws. Every inch of it is private ranch land, so stay on the road and don't climb the fences; people do, and it is why the loop nearly gets closed every few years.
gear: patience — it is slow going in bloom season

drive.scenicNote: Out the bottom of the loop and down RR 1323 into Fredericksburg for the night.
